name: In-situ low-temperature Raman spectroscopy on a Linkam THMS600 liquid-nitrogen stage
plain_name: Study a sample using light at low temperature

sources.citation: Park, H., Wang, A., Kim, J., Pophali, A., Gersappe, D., Kim, T. (2026). Molecular-level freezing and melting dynamics of aqueous lithium chloride solutions using in-situ Raman spectroscopy. Scientific Reports 16, 32309.

Pamula, K., Pophali, A., Gersappe, D., Kim, T. (2025). In-situ Raman spectroscopic analysis of phase transition temperatures in silica interacting with water and NaCl solutions. Scientific Reports 15, 26449.

reported_conditions.as_printed: liquid nitrogen pumped from a dewar
liquid nitrogen, Linkam D2L/80 dewar, LNP96 pump

requirements.rationale: Park et al. (2026) cooled to −140 °C, the lowest point of that paper's freezing/melting cycles; this is the paper's choice set by the phase behaviour studied, and the user confirms −140 °C as the required operating point.
Raman scattering is collected through the stage window with a microscope objective in both sources; optical access to the cold sample is intrinsic to the technique.

Park et al. (2026) and Pamula et al. (2025) load the sample in a 15 mm diameter quartz crucible inside the stage, so the stage must accept a 15 mm sample; this is the papers' sample format, confirmed by the user.

Pamula et al. (2025) focus through the stage with a 6.5 mm working-distance objective. The working distance that the stage window geometry requires must not exceed the objective's 6.5 mm, so a stage requiring more than 6.5 mm would be incompatible with this optical setup. Non-mandatory because a longer-WD objective could be substituted.

missing_information: stage window material and thickness not stated
objective used by Park et al. not stated
purge gas / condensation control not stated
THMS600 specified temperature range not stated in either paper (only ranges used)
confirmation_note: Requirements reviewed and confirmed by the profile author on 2026-10-31 against the quoted evidence records. Any edited value must be re-confirmed by the user before the profile is used.
